channel.title: Blog Demagogues
channel.description: Essays about books, and occasionally at each other.

item.title: On being told what to think by a butler
item.description: Ishiguro's Stevens is not a tragic figure. He is a colleague. Every office has one, and most of us have been him.

item.title: Stevens cannot say what he means
item.description: The Remains of the Day is built out of sentences that circle their subject without landing on it. A close reading of three of them.

item.title: The slow first hundred pages, defended
item.description: Middlemarch does not begin so much as accumulate. That is the point, and it is the part everyone skips.

item.title: Everyone I know is reading the same twelve books
item.description: On the strange narrowing of what counts as a book worth mentioning at dinner.
